prize_parts.citation: for turning targeted protein degradation into a designable chemical modality, through PROTACs and the molecular mechanism of glue degraders

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the one candidate that five of us placed in the top three, and the support holds up when I ask my own question: was the mechanism actually determined? Here it was. Crystal structures of ternary complexes (VHL and cereblon with ligand and target) explain selectivity and cooperativity, and the cereblon-thalidomide structural and biochemical work by Handa and colleagues turned an empirical drug into a mechanistically understood molecular glue. Crews and Deshaies established the heterobifunctional concept; Handa supplies the mechanistic anchor for glues. The result is a new design principle, induced proximity through an E3 ligase, that chemists now apply to targets previously considered undruggable. I moved this to first place from my opening second rank because the colleagues' arguments on breadth and independent confirmation are stronger than my own attachment to the porous-materials candidate.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved yet, so the claim of impact is still partly prospective, and the prize would honour a modality rather than a finished therapy. The three-name cut also leaves out Ciulli, whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex structural work made PROTACs drug-like, and Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito. If Handa is chosen, the glue half of the citation rests on one mechanistic discovery while the PROTAC half is shared by two people, which is lopsided as a single achievement.

responses.point: Linke ranks phase separation first as an elegant physical principle and finds degraders plausible but possibly a little early because no PROTAC drug is approved.
responses.response: I accept the timing concern as real but not decisive. The chemical principle and its structural basis are already confirmed by many independent groups, and the prize rewards the discovery, not the approval date. I am less comfortable with phase separation as first choice. For specific in vivo condensates the interpretation is still contested, and I would want evidence that the molecular-level structure of the interactions, not only the droplet phenomenology, is established. That is the standard I apply to any claimed mechanism, and B014 meets it less cleanly than B036.

responses.point: Aili puts degraders first because bifunctional molecules and glues make ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis a designable chemical modality for undruggable targets, and he also ranks halide perovskites second.
responses.response: I agree on degraders and want to add the structural argument, since it is what makes the modality designable rather than lucky. Ternary-complex crystal structures show why some degraders are selective and cooperative, and that is the basis for rational design. I do not share the enthusiasm for perovskites as a prize now. The efficiencies are certified, but stability and lead toxicity are unresolved, and the credit is split across at least six people, so a trio would be hard to defend. I keep it below the top tier.

responses.point: Somfai ranks palladium-catalysed C-N coupling first as a fully mature, daily-use reaction, and treats Kosugi as a precursor so that Buchwald and Hartwig are the core pair.
responses.response: I agree with his attribution reading: Buchwald and Hartwig carried the catalyst design and mechanistic work, and Kosugi's tin-amide chemistry was not general. My reservation is novelty of concept. After the 2010 cross-coupling prize, a C-N variant is a refinement of an already honoured paradigm, and the committee would have to explain why now. I put it clearly behind degraders but regard it as a serious alternative if we want a prize for established synthetic methodology.

responses.point: Chabes ranks degraders first and notes that Ciulli, Gray and others made major later contributions, so a three-person cut leaves out real contributors.
responses.response: I agree that the cut is hard, and I would qualify his own proposal slightly. Crews and Deshaies conceived PROTACs and Handa identified cereblon, so these three are the originating discoveries. Ciulli's contribution is closer to enabling refinement and structural rationalisation, which is important but later. I would be open to Ciulli replacing Handa if the committee decides the prize should be about the PROTAC design principle rather than both PROTACs and glues.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks long-range electron transfer through proteins first for its quantitative physical treatment, and ranks degraders only seventh.
responses.response: Gray and Winkler's work is rigorous and mature, and I respect the time-resolved kinetics. But the theoretical core, Marcus and tunnelling-pathway theory, was largely recognised earlier or sits outside the credited pair, so the new prize would honour a refinement of a recognised framework. Degraders open a new capability with real consequences for medicine, and I see no reason to rank the more incremental physical-chemistry claim above it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers Handa (glue mechanism) or Ciulli (structural basis of ternary complexes) as the third laureate, and whether the citation should span both PROTACs and glues.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes the recognition premature compared with mature alternatives.
Whether my continued interest in B017 (mesoporous silica) is a field bias, given the unresolved Mobil versus FSM-16 priority question and the recent porous-materials prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. My field overlaps with porous materials (B017), and I am a Stockholm University colleague of the Secretary, but neither is a personal or institutional connection to the proposed laureates.
